newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria starts to reopen Nembe oil wells.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria starts to reopen Nembe oil wells.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's local unit said on Wednesday it had begun reopening five flow stations shut since Sunday because of a communal feud in oil-producing southeastern Nigeria.

"We had a meeting with community leaders in Nembe this morning and began reopening some wells around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT)," a Shell spokesman said in Lagos. "We will progressively reopen all the wells over the next two days."
Armed youths went to Shell's flow stations in Nembe on Sunday and told its staff to leave in protest over the sharing of relief materials donated to the community during previous unrest.
Shell said the closure shut in about 120,000 barrels per day of crude but that exports were continuing normally.

The Anglo-Dutch company, the biggest oil operator in Nigeria, is frequently the target of local communities angry that they do not benefit from the proceeds of the commodity pumped from their backyard. --Lagos newsroom +234 1 2630317
